reader_question: What do public schools spend, and where does the money come from?
grade_line: Documented: the Census Bureau’s survey of public school system finances, fiscal 2024
title: Public school systems spent $17,619 a pupil in fiscal 2024, and 88 cents of each dollar they took in came from state and local sources.
measure_line: Revenue by source, current spending per pupil and enrollment of every public school system in the 50 states and DC, fiscal 2024, the 2023 to 2024 school year
notes: Federal revenue includes $39.2 billion in one-time COVID-19 relief, which Oath & Action summed over every school system from the Census Bureau’s file of all its data items; it is part of the federal 12 cents.
The Census Bureau counts every public school system, including those a state, county or city runs, and leaves out charter schools whose charter a private group holds.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Annual Survey of School System Finances, Tables 1, 5, 8, 11 and 19, fiscal 2024, public school systems, United States. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Federal revenue includes $39.2 billion in COVID-19 relief funds.
alt: Six facts on what public school systems took in and spent in fiscal 2024, each with the Census Bureau table it comes from.

facts.words: came to public school systems from federal, state and local sources.
of each dollar came from the states, 43 cents from local sources, mostly property taxes, and 12 cents from the federal government.

for each pupil went to current spending, the day-to-day cost of running schools, which leaves out construction and equipment, interest on debt, payments to other governments, adult education and community services.
for each pupil in New York was the most among the 50 states and DC.
for each pupil in Idaho was the least.
students were enrolled in fall 2023, the count each per-pupil figure divides by.
